holidays.name: National Kangaroo Awareness Day
holidays.description: Pull on your boxing gloves, or just your hopping shoes, and give some love to Australia's most famous bouncer. The day is for learning about kangaroos, the challenges they face in the wild, and why these pouched marvels deserve a little more attention.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a favorite on quirky-holiday calendars for animal lovers.
holidays.funFact: Kangaroos can't easily walk backward because of their large feet and powerful tails. That's one reason they appear on Australia's coat of arms, which symbolizes a country always moving forward.

holidays.name: National Food Day
holidays.description: A day for thinking about what's on your plate. It encourages people to enjoy fresh, affordable, sustainably produced food and to support healthier food policies. Try a new vegetable, visit a farmers market, or cook a meal from scratch.
holidays.origin: The Center for Science in the Public Interest launched Food Day in 1975 as a day of education and action around food issues. It was revived as a nationwide movement in 2011 and is now marked each October 24.
holidays.funFact: Food Day was first held in the 1970s as a teach-in style event, and the modern version has drawn thousands of events across the U.S., including school lunches, community dinners, and garden projects.
